facts.fact: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform is Google Cloud's AI and agent platform (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

Vertex AI was renamed Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (Agent Platform) on 2026-04-22, and old bookmarked links redirect (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

Memory Bank was renamed Agent Platform Memory Bank in the 2026-04-22 Agent Platform rename (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Vertex AI Model Garden was renamed Model Garden in the 2026-04-22 Agent Platform rename (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

The Agent Platform docs are organized into four pillars: Build (ADK, Agent Garden, Agent Studio, Skill Registry, RAG Engine, Vector Search, Managed Agents API), Scale (Agent Runtime, Sessions, Memory Bank), Govern (Agent Gateway, semantic governance, content security, Identity and IAM) and Optimize (evaluation, observability, traces, topology, simulated evaluations, online monitoring, prompt optimization) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/overview).
Agent Gateway is part of the Govern pillar of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/overview).
The underlying API host was kept through the rename: the Agent Platform service is still aiplatform.googleapis.com (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime).
Agent Runtime instances are still the ReasoningEngine API resource 'for backward compatibility' after the rename (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime).
Model Garden lists Gemini, Veo and Lyria, partner models (Claude, Grok, Mistral) and open models (Llama, DeepSeek, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs).
Claude is listed in Model Garden as a partner model alongside Grok and Mistral (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs).

Agent Runtime (formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine) is a managed runtime for deploying, operating and scaling agents that supports any language or framework that can be containerized and follows the runtime contract (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime).
Agent Runtime has full ADK integration: Python via the adk CLI and Go via the adkgo CLI (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime).

Agent Runtime provides managed SDK templates for LangChain, LangGraph, AG2 and LlamaIndex, while CrewAI and custom frameworks use a custom template (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime).
The adk CLI (Python) and adkgo CLI (Go) deploy ADK agents to Agent Runtime (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime).

On 2026-04-22 Agent Runtime added long-running operations of up to 7 days, sub-second cold starts, provisioning in under 1 minute, bring-your-own-container (BYOC) and custom session IDs (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Agent Runtime agent revisions and traffic splitting entered preview on 2026-05-19 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

Agent Runtime accepts three deployment inputs: a prebuilt image in Artifact Registry, a Dockerfile plus source (Agent Runtime builds the image), or the legacy Python package spec (a pickled agent agent.pkl plus requirements.txt in Cloud Storage) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/use-terraform ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime).
Agent Runtime can deploy a prebuilt container image stored in Artifact Registry (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/use-terraform).

The legacy Agent Runtime Python package spec reads a pickled agent.pkl plus requirements.txt from Cloud Storage (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/use-terraform).

facts.fact: Memory Bank IngestEvents went GA on 2026-07-08, memory profiles went GA on 2026-07-15, and Memory Bank got a console page on 2026-11-06 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Gemini 3.5 Flash became the default Memory Bank generation model on 2026-06-29 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Memory Bank and Sessions accept the global, us and eu locations (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/agent-locations).

Agent Platform Sessions and Memory Bank provide managed short-term and long-term agent memory, and Sessions accepts the global, us and eu locations (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/agent-locations).

Agent Runtime includes a code-execution sandbox, reached through the SDK module client.sandboxes, with its own quotas (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/agent-quotas).
Agent Development Kit (ADK) is Google's open-source, code-first agent framework, available in Python, Go, Java, TypeScript and Kotlin (https://adk.dev/llms.txt).
The latest ADK Python release is google-adk 2.14.1, published 2026-11-12 (https://pypi.org/project/google-adk/).
ADK supports deployment to Agent Runtime, Cloud Run and GKE (https://adk.dev/llms.txt).
ADK agents can be deployed to GKE as well as Agent Runtime and Cloud Run (https://adk.dev/llms.txt).

RAG Engine (formerly Vertex AI RAG Engine) is the managed RAG pipeline in Agent Platform covering ingest, chunking, embedding, indexing into a corpus, retrieval and grounded generation, with local files, Cloud Storage and Google Drive as data sources (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/rag-engine/rag-overview).
RAG Engine supports VPC Service Controls and CMEK, but not data residency or AXT controls (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/rag-engine/rag-overview).

RAG Engine regions are restricted: us-central1, us-east4, us-east1 and europe-west1 need an allowlist for new projects (existing projects unaffected), europe-west3 and europe-west4 are GA, and most other regions are Preview (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/rag-engine/rag-overview).
RAG Engine's backing store is a RAG Engine-managed Spanner instance, billed in GA locations (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/rag-engine/rag-overview).

Agent Search (formerly Vertex AI Search), the managed enterprise search and grounding product, runs on the Discovery Engine API (discoveryengine.googleapis.com) (https://cloud.google.com/products/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/agent-search).

Agent Search data stores are structured or unstructured, and connectors either federate (query the source live) or ingest (copy into the index) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/introduction-to-connectors-and-data-stores).

The Gen AI evaluation service scores models and agents with adaptive rubrics (per-prompt pass/fail tests), with GENERAL_QUALITY as the recommended default metric (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/evaluation-overview).

Gen AI evaluation service agent metrics are final_response_quality, final_response_reference_free, hallucination and tool_use_quality (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/determine-eval).

The Gen AI evaluation SDK flow is generate_rubrics(), then run_inference(), then evaluate(), and the SDK interface is marked Preview in places (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/evaluation-overview).
OpenTelemetry tracing has been on by default for newly deployed ADK agents on Agent Runtime since 2026-06-18 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Agents built with ADK 2.6.0 or later can emit gen_ai telemetry metrics to Cloud Monitoring (2026-08-13) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Agent Observability, which includes MCP server health, went GA on 2026-06-18 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

Agent Registry, a catalog of agents, MCP servers and tools, endpoints and skills, entered public preview on 2026-04-22 and went GA on 2026-06-18 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Agent Registry supports A2A protocol 1.0 (supportedInterfaces) alongside the 0.3 schema (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Registration in Agent Registry needs the Agent Registry API enabled in a governance project (https://docs.cloud.google.com/agent-registry/overview).

Agent Gateway is the policy enforcement point for agent ingress (Client-to-Agent) and egress (Agent-to-Anywhere) traffic, covering LLM, MCP and A2A traffic (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview).

Agent Gateway enforces IAM Unified Access Policies (deny by default), Model Armor and semantic governance policies (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview).
Agent Gateway enforces Model Armor policies on governed agent traffic (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview).

Agent Gateway is available for Agent Runtime and Gemini Enterprise; cross-cloud Kubernetes support entered Limited Preview on 2026-11-11, and GKE and Cloud Run support are in early preview (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Agent Gateway is available for Gemini Enterprise as well as Agent Runtime (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview).

Agent Gateway cross-cloud Kubernetes support entered Limited Preview on 2026-11-11, and GKE and Cloud Run support are in early preview (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Each Agent Gateway can govern up to 5,000 registered resources (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview).
Agent Gateway covers LLM, MCP and A2A traffic (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/gateways/agent-gateway-overview).

facts.fact: Skill Registry entered preview on 2026-05-19 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
The Managed Agents API entered preview on 2026-05-19 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

The Agent Identity API (agentidentity.googleapis.com) entered preview on 2026-06-18 and replaces the legacy IAM Connectors API during a migration period (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
BigQuery's managed AI functions are AI.IF, AI.CLASSIFY and AI.SCORE, and BigQuery picks the model for them (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/generative-ai-overview).
BigQuery's general-purpose AI functions are AI.GENERATE and AI.GENERATE_TABLE, which take a custom output schema (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/generative-ai-overview).
BigQuery managed and general-purpose AI functions call Agent Platform models and incur their charges (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/generative-ai-overview).
BigQuery data agents run on the Conversational Analytics API (geminidataanalytics.googleapis.com) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/conversational-analytics-api/release-notes).

The Conversational Analytics API went GA for BigQuery and Looker on 2026-06-23 and offers v1 REST endpoints (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/conversational-analytics-api/release-notes).
The Conversational Analytics API is GA for both BigQuery and Looker since 2026-06-23 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/conversational-analytics-api/release-notes).

Conversational Analytics API BigQuery Graph data sources went GA on 2026-09-30, Deep Dive thinking mode entered Preview on 2026-09-03, and AlloyDB, Cloud SQL and Spanner data sources entered Preview on 2026-03-30 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/conversational-analytics-api/release-notes).

Agents publish to Gemini Enterprise, for example via agents-cli publish gemini-enterprise; Gemini API / AI Studio, Gemini Enterprise, Google Workspace and Gemini CLI integration are covered in a separate note (https://google.github.io/agents-cli/guide/getting-started/index.md).
agents-cli publish gemini-enterprise publishes an agent to Gemini Enterprise (https://google.github.io/agents-cli/guide/getting-started/index.md).
This research found no dedicated Agent Platform computer-use or browser-use runtime (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs).

The Agent Platform REST API global host is https://aiplatform.googleapis.com, regional hosts follow https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com, and the multi-region jurisdictions are us and eu (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/data-residency).
The Agent Platform eu multi-region jurisdiction excludes the UK and Switzerland (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/data-residency).

Agent Platform REST calls authenticate with an OAuth 2.0 bearer token (gcloud auth print-access-token) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/use-claude).

facts.target: Agent Platform express mode API key
facts.fact: In express mode, Agent Platform REST calls can authenticate with an API key instead of an OAuth 2.0 token (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/data-residency).

Claude on Agent Platform is called through rawPredict and streamRawPredict at POST https://LOCATION-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/LOCATION/publishers/anthropic/models/MODEL:rawPredict with "anthropic_version": "vertex-2023-10-16" in the body and model IDs like claude-sonnet-4-6 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/use-claude).
You must click Enable on each Claude model's Model Garden card before calling it (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/use-claude).

The Anthropic SDK for Agent Platform is installed with pip install -U 'anthropic[vertex]' and used through the AnthropicVertex(project_id=..., region=...) client (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/use-claude).

Claude on Agent Platform supports client tools (function calling), but the page says 'Server tools are not supported' (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/use-claude).
The anthropic package was at 2.8.0 on PyPI as of 2026-11-10 (https://pypi.org/project/anthropic/).
The anthropic[vertex] SDK is Anthropic's SDK for calling Claude on Agent Platform (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/use-claude).

Google Gen AI SDK packages are Python google-genai, JS/TS @google/genai, Go google.golang.org/genai, Java com.google.genai:google-genai and .NET Google.GenAI (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/sdks/overview).
The Python google-genai package was at 3.3.0 on 2026-11-12 (https://pypi.org/project/google-genai/).

Configure the Google Gen AI SDK for Agent Platform with GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION=global and GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE=True (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/sdks/overview).
GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE is the new name for GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI, and the two are equivalent (https://adk.dev/get-started/google-cloud/).
Older ADK versions recognize only GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI, so set it or upgrade ADK if GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE doesn't connect (https://adk.dev/get-started/google-cloud/).

In google-cloud-aiplatform 2.0.1 (2026-09-18), a breaking change, agent surfaces moved into the separate package google-cloud-agentplatform (imported as agentplatform), generative modules moved to google-genai, and vertexai.agent_engines maps to agentplatform.Client().runtimes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

Code uses agentplatform.Client(project=..., location=...) with .runtimes, .sessions, .sandboxes and .memory_banks to work with Agent Runtime and its memory (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime).
Both google-cloud-agentplatform and google-cloud-aiplatform were at 2.9.0 on 2026-11-12 (https://pypi.org/project/google-cloud-agentplatform/).

facts.fact: MCP Toolbox for Databases (googleapis/mcp-toolbox) is the new name of genai-toolbox (Gen AI Toolbox for Databases), Google's open-source MCP server for databases (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).
The latest MCP Toolbox for Databases release is v1.17.0 (2026-11-13) (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).

MCP Toolbox sources include AlloyDB, BigQuery, Cloud SQL, Spanner, Firestore and Knowledge Catalog, plus PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB, Redis, Snowflake, Neo4j, ClickHouse, Trino and others (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).
MCP Toolbox docs are at https://mcp-toolbox.dev/ (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).

MCP Toolbox runs from a binary, npx or Go with stdio or HTTP transport; the Windows binary is https://storage.googleapis.com/mcp-toolbox-for-databases/v1.17.0/windows/amd64/toolbox.exe, and HTTP runs on default port 5000 at /mcp or /mcp/{toolset} (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).
npx -y @toolbox-sdk/server --prebuilt=bigquery --stdio runs the prebuilt BigQuery MCP Toolbox over stdio, and custom tools go in --config tools.yaml (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).

MCP Toolbox client SDKs: Python toolbox-core, toolbox-langchain and toolbox-llamaindex; JS @toolbox-sdk/core and @toolbox-sdk/adk; Go github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox-sdk-go; Java com.google.cloud.mcp:mcp-toolbox-sdk-java (https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox).
toolbox-core was at 1.4.0 on 2026-09-01 (https://pypi.org/project/toolbox-core/).

ADK agents call external MCP servers through McpToolset with connection classes StdioConnectionParams, StreamableHTTPConnectionParams and SseConnectionParams; MCP is supported in Python, TypeScript (MCPToolset), Go, Java and Kotlin (https://adk.dev/tools-custom/mcp-tools/).
Production ADK agents must define McpToolset synchronously in agent.py (https://adk.dev/tools-custom/mcp-tools/).
Cloud Run hosts custom MCP servers over Streamable HTTP but not stdio (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/host-mcp-servers).

Clients of a Cloud Run-hosted MCP server authenticate with Cloud Run Invoker via gcloud run services proxy NAME --region REGION --port=3000, an OIDC ID token, or IAP (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/host-mcp-servers).
Deploying to Cloud Run with --functional-type=mcp-server registers the MCP server in Agent Registry automatically (https://docs.cloud.google.com/agent-registry/register-mcp-servers).

Agent Runtime lists A2A deployment as supported, with A2A multi-agent systems marked preview; A2A is also supported on Cloud Run and Agent Registry (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/build/runtime).
A2A agents serve /.well-known/agent-card.json, which Agent Registry reads to extract skills (https://docs.cloud.google.com/agent-registry/register-mcp-servers).
ADK consumes remote A2A agents through RemoteA2aAgent (https://codelabs.developers.google.com/adk-a2a-agent-runtime).
adkgo deploy cloudrun enables --a2a by default (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/).

A2A methods on Agent Runtime have their own quotas: POST methods (sendMessage, cancelTask) at 60 per minute and GET methods (getTask, getCard) at 600 per minute (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/agent-quotas).

Apigee hosts MCP servers for existing APIs through the MCP Discovery Proxy: each OpenAPI 3.0.0-3.0.3 operation becomes an MCP tool behind ORG_NAME.mcp.apigee.internal, using JSON-RPC tools/list and tools/call (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).
The Apigee MCP Discovery Proxy authenticates with OAuth 2.1 or OIDC (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).

Apigee MCP is available on Subscription, Pay-as-you-go, Evaluation and Data Residency organizations, and on Apigee hybrid 1.17.0 or later (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).

The Apigee API hub MCP server went GA on 2026-07-24, with endpoints https://apihub.googleapis.com/mcp (global) and https://apihub.REGION.rep.googleapis.com/mcp (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/apihub/release-notes).
The Apigee API hub MCP server integrates with Model Armor (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/apihub/release-notes).

gcloud apihub locations configure-and-deploy-server (2026-08-12), like the ConfigureAndDeployServer RPC (2026-07-24), bundles API operations into MCP servers deployed on Apigee (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/apihub/release-notes).
API hub syncs MCP metadata to Agent Registry by default (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/apihub/register-mcp-apis).

ADK reaches Application Integration and Integration Connectors through the Python class google.adk.tools.application_integration_tool.application_integration_toolset.ApplicationIntegrationToolset (with a Java equivalent), using integration= with triggers for workflows (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).
ApplicationIntegrationToolset uses connection= with entity_operations and actions for Integration Connectors (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).
ApplicationIntegrationToolset needs roles/integrations.integrationEditor, roles/connectors.invoker and roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).
ApplicationIntegrationToolset needs roles/connectors.invoker to call Integration Connectors (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).
ApplicationIntegrationToolset needs roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).

Integration Connectors has 147 connectors, 35 for Google services and 112 for other applications, with GA connectors including Salesforce, ServiceNow, Snowflake, SharePoint, Workday, Microsoft Dynamics 365 and the SAP family (ERP, HANA, SuccessFactors, Ariba) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/integration-connectors/docs/connector-reference-overview).
Databricks was not listed among Integration Connectors connectors (https://docs.cloud.google.com/integration-connectors/docs/connector-reference-overview).

facts.fact: Integration Connectors added an MCP connector (client side) in preview on 2025-12-16 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/integration-connectors/docs/release-notes).

The Integration Connectors MCP connector has versions v1 and v2 for MCP API versions and allocates 2 nodes per connection by default (https://docs.cloud.google.com/integration-connectors/docs/connectors/mcp/overview-mcp).
The MCP connector is used from Application Integration via the Connectors task (https://docs.cloud.google.com/integration-connectors/docs/connectors/mcp/overview-mcp).

The Conversational Analytics API has native SDKs in seven languages: Python, Java, Go, Node.js, PHP, Ruby and .NET (https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/build-data-agents-with-conversational-analytics-api).
The Conversational Analytics API global endpoint is geminidataanalytics.googleapis.com (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/data-agents/conversational-analytics-api/data-residency).
gcloud run deploy --source . builds and deploys from source, and --image deploys an existing image (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/).
Cloud Run services are private by default unless --allow-unauthenticated is set (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/).
Authenticated Cloud Run calls use Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-identity-token) (https://adk.dev/deploy/cloud-run/).

Install the gcloud CLI on Windows with winget install --id Google.CloudSDK (version 593.0.0 on winget as of 2026-11-14) or the installer https://dl.google.com/dl/cloudsdk/channels/rapid/GoogleCloudSDKInstaller.exe (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install-sdk).
The gcloud CLI on Windows needs Windows 8.1+ or Server 2012+, supports Python 3.10-3.15 and bundles Python by default (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install-sdk).
The current gcloud CLI is 593.0.0, released 2026-11-10; release 591.0.0 updated bundled Python to 3.14.9 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/release-notes).
In gcloud 593.0.0, bundled Python became a required component on Windows x86/x86_64 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/release-notes).
gcloud init authorizes and creates a default configuration (--console-only skips the browser), and gcloud auth login signs in the CLI itself (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install-sdk).
gcloud auth application-default login creates the separate ADC file that client libraries, ADK and MCP clients use (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials).

ADC searches in a fixed order: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, then the gcloud ADC file, then the attached service account via the metadata server (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials).

The ADC file is %APPDATA%\gcloud\application_default_credentials.json on Windows and $HOME/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json on Linux and macOS (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials).
ADC user tokens expire about every hour (https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/configure-mcp-ai-application).

Service account impersonation is set per command with --impersonate-service-account=SA_EMAIL, for the whole CLI with gcloud config set auth/impersonate_service_account SA_EMAIL, or for ADC with gcloud auth application-default login --impersonate-service-account SA_EMAIL (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/use-service-account-impersonation).
Service account impersonation needs roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on the target service account (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/use-service-account-impersonation).
Service account impersonation needs iamcredentials.googleapis.com enabled (https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/use-service-account-impersonation).

gcloud command groups for agent work are gcloud ai (models, endpoints, semantic-governance-policies GA in 581.0.0), gcloud agent-registry (skills, revisions, publishers and findings GA in 591.0.0), gcloud agent-identity auth-providers (authorizations GA in 593.0.0), gcloud run deploy and gcloud services enable (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/release-notes).

The old gcloud MCP command groups were removed in favor of Agent Registry: gcloud api-registry mcp enable|disable (579.0.0), gcloud beta services mcp enable|disable|list (581.0.0), and gcloud api-registry mcp servers list|tools list and gcloud beta services mcp policies (582.0.0) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/release-notes).

facts.fact: MCP reference pages are the overview at https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/overview and the endpoint list at https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/supported-products (https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/supported-products).
The Google Cloud status page is https://status.cloud.google.com/, which resolved on 2026-11-14 (https://status.cloud.google.com/).

Official samples and codelabs include github.com/google/adk-python (v2.14.1, 2026-11-12), github.com/google/agents-cli, github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox and the codelab https://codelabs.developers.google.com/adk-a2a-agent-runtime (A2A on Agent Runtime) (https://github.com/google/adk-python ; https://codelabs.developers.google.com/adk-a2a-agent-runtime).
The Agents CLI codelab is https://codelabs.developers.google.com/agents-cli-agent-platform/agents-cli-agent-platform (https://github.com/google/adk-python).

Standard PayGo replaced dynamic shared quota as the documented model for Gemini on Agent Platform, and the old /vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/dsq URL now serves the Standard PayGo page (https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/dsq).

Under Standard PayGo, Gemini usage runs on shared capacity with an organization-level usage tier set by eligible spend over a rolling 30 days (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/standard-paygo).
A Standard PayGo tier's TPM threshold is the level below which traffic is prioritized, not a hard cap (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/standard-paygo).

Standard PayGo TPM thresholds as shown 2026-11-14: Pro, Carbon and Argon get Tier 1 ($10-$250) 500K, Tier 2 ($250-$2,000) 1M, Tier 3 ($2,000-$50,000) 2M and Tier 4 (above $50,000) 10M; Flash, Flash-Lite and Hydrogen get 2M, 4M, 10M and 50M; there is no separate RPM limit and preview models are excluded (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/standard-paygo).
Standard PayGo Tier 4 was added on 2026-09-10 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

A 429 on Standard PayGo means temporary contention for shared capacity, not an exhausted fixed quota; the fixes are exponential backoff, smoothing per-second spikes, and using the global endpoint (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/standard-paygo).

For Gemini, the global endpoint draws on a worldwide pool and gets the full tier threshold but gives no data residency guarantee; multi-region us and eu use separate pools; single-region endpoints such as us-central1 have the least headroom; Google recommends global unless residency requires otherwise (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/standard-paygo).
Org policy can block global endpoint traffic on Agent Platform (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/data-residency).

Gemini models older than Gemini 3 are not served on the jurisdictional multi-region endpoints and stay on regional endpoints, and calling a model at an endpoint type it does not support returns a 404 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/data-residency ; https://www.braintrust.dev/docs/kb/vertex-ai-gemini-model-region-and-registry-issues.md (secondary)).

Priority PayGo (preview) costs more per token than Standard PayGo but gives more consistent throughput, with no commitment, and responses report ON_DEMAND_PRIORITY as the traffic type (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/priority-paygo).
Priority PayGo ramp limits were removed on 2026-09-10 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
Priority PayGo endpoint support (global, or global plus us/eu) differs between page versions (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/priority-paygo).
Flex PayGo (preview) is 50% off Standard PayGo, for latency-tolerant work (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/flex-paygo).

Flex PayGo works only on the global endpoint, allows a 20 MB payload, and accepts request timeouts up to 30 minutes (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/deploy/flex-paygo).

Provisioned Throughput is bought in GSUs (generative AI scale units) for terms of 1 week, 1 month, 3 months or 1 year (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/provisioned-throughput/use-provisioned-throughput).

Provisioned Throughput quota is GSUs times the model's per-GSU throughput, for example 2,690 tokens/s per GSU for gemini-2.5-flash and 685 tokens/s for Gemini 4 Hydrogen, enforced over a 1 to 120 second window depending on order size (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/provisioned-throughput/use-provisioned-throughput).

By default a request over the Provisioned Throughput quota spills over in full to pay-as-you-go billing; send header X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Request-Type: dedicated to get a 429 instead of overage charges, or shared to bypass Provisioned Throughput (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/provisioned-throughput/use-provisioned-throughput).

facts.fact: Claude models launched after 2026-05-26 share one quota per lineage per location (anthropic-claude-opus, -sonnet, -haiku, -fable and -fable-fast); global, us and eu are separate buckets, fast-mode requests use a *-fast bucket, and older Claude models use per-model QPM/TPM by endpoint type (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).

Default Claude Opus 5.5 quota as shown 2026-11-14 is 2,000 QPM, 20M input TPM and 2M output TPM on global, and half that on multi-region (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).

Default Claude Sonnet 5.5/5 quota as shown 2026-11-14 is 2,500 QPM, 25M input TPM and 2.5M output TPM on global (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).

Default Claude Sonnet 5.5/5 quota as shown 2026-11-14 is 2,500 QPM, 25M input TPM and 2.5M output TPM on global (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).

Default Claude Haiku 5.5 quota as shown 2026-11-14 is 3,000 QPM, 30M input TPM and 3M output TPM on global (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).
The Quota page's Claude token usage can be inaccurate, so use the token_count metrics (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/partner-models/claude/quotas).

New projects can show Claude quota as '0 to 0' until model access eligibility is reviewed (https://discuss.google.dev/t/anthropic-claude-quota-stuck-at-0-to-0-on-new-paid-account-requesting-manual-model-access-eligibility-review-eu-multi-region/382201 (secondary)).

Agent Runtime default quotas per project per region: Query/StreamQuery 90 per minute, BidiStreamQuery 10 concurrent live connections, 100 resources, resource create/update/delete 10 per minute, session writes 100 per minute, session event appends 300 per minute, and 950 revisions per agent (a fixed system limit) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/agent-quotas).
Agent Runtime express mode allows only 10 query requests per minute and 10 resources (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/resources/agent-quotas).

RAG Engine quotas per project per region: data-management APIs 60 RPM, RetrievalContexts 600 RPM, ImportRagFiles 3 concurrent and 10,000 files per request (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/quotas).
The Gen AI evaluation service quota is 1,000 RPM and 20 concurrent runs per project per region (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/quotas).
Agent Platform online inference quota is 30,000 RPM and CRUD calls 600 RPM per project per region (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/machine-learning/quotas).

BigQuery MCP SQL tools cancel queries after 3 minutes by default, return at most 3,000 rows, and don't support Google Drive external tables; BigQuery API quotas still apply (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/use-bigquery-mcp).
execute_sql_readonly on the BigQuery MCP server rejects DML, DDL, Python UDFs and GQL (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/use-bigquery-mcp).

Cloud Run limits: requests up to 60 minutes; HTTP/1 requests and responses capped at 32 MiB (except HTTP/2 and streamed responses); up to 1,000 concurrent requests, 32 GiB memory and 8 vCPU per instance; default regional cap of 100 instances per project; L4 GPU quota 0 by default (3 auto-granted to new projects) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/quotas).
Apigee SaaS organizations are capped at 1,000 MCP tools (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).
Apigee MCP provisioning may fail in europe-central2, europe-southwest1, europe-west9 and me-central2 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).

GET requests on Apigee MCP error responses return 405 because SSE is not supported; Apigee hybrid does not support the stateless MCP protocol 2026-07-28, and toggling MCP there triggers a staged Message Processor restart (https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-platform/apigee-mcp/apigee-mcp-overview).

Container-based Agent Runtime deploys need the Agent Runtime service agent to have Artifact Registry Reader; without it, pods fail with IMAGE_PULL_BACKOFF (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/runtime/use-terraform).

Do not grant roles/integrations.integrationInvoker to ADK agents on Agent Runtime that use ApplicationIntegrationToolset: the docs say it can cause 403 errors and list roles/integrations.integrationEditor instead (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).

Granting roles/integrations.integrationInvoker to ADK agents on Agent Runtime that use ApplicationIntegrationToolset can cause 403 errors; use roles/integrations.integrationEditor (https://adk.dev/integrations/application-integration/).

Hand-pasted ADC bearer tokens in MCP client configs expire after about an hour; for long-lived clients use an OAuth client or authProviderType: google_credentials (https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/configure-mcp-ai-application).
Model Armor prompt-injection filters can produce false-positive 403s on the Developer Knowledge MCP server, and HIGH_AND_ABOVE confidence is recommended (https://developers.google.com/knowledge/mcp).

The SDK split in google-cloud-aiplatform 2.0.1 breaks code that imports vertexai.agent_engines or the vertexai generative modules; migrate to google-cloud-agentplatform and google-genai (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).
A 2026-03-31 security fix requires google-cloud-aiplatform >= 1.165.1 or an explicit staging bucket (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes).

Application Integration announced on 2026-08-28 a change to how identities are handled for integration runs, which may require customer action (https://docs.cloud.google.com/application-integration/docs/release-notes).
